newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold down as bullion slips, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold down as bullion slips, others mixed.

text.p: Yen-denominated Tokyo gold futures ended lower across the board on Friday, depressed by a continued slide in bullion prices, while other precious metals were mixed, traders said.
TOCOM most-active December gold futures closed eight yen lower at 1,342 yen per gram. The remaining months were six yen to 13 yen lower.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted lower at $344.75/5.25 an ounce, extending an overnight loss after New York's close of $345.35/85 on Thursday and Tokyo's close of $350.30/60 on Thursday.

"Spot gold was under heavy selling pressure during Asian hours," one dealer at a foreign bank said. "Australian producers were thought to be in a hurry to sell gold, taking advantage of rises in Australian-based gold prices following dips in Australian dollar," he said.

Japanese trade houses were forced to sell TOCOM gold, pressured by a continued slide in bullion prices, while some bargain-hunting buying by individual investors prevented prices from dipping further, the traders said.
With sentiment toward gold bullion remaining bearish, the next support was pinned at $342.00, one trader said.
Platinum futures rebounded from early lows as the dollar crawled back above 122 yen in late Tokyo.
Uncertainty over the near-term currency market limited interest in platinum, traders said.
TOCOM December platinum ended up two at 1,358 yen a gram. December silver was up 2.0 yen at 192.9 yen per 10 grams.
TOCOM December palladium was up two yen at 471 yen per gram, although spot February was down seven at 472 yen in a correction of the previous day's gains.
